task_message:
Case M34: segment the myxoid soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 240x240x480 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case M34 is complete. Final mask saved (v2): a single connected component, 26.7 mL.

**What was segmented:** An elongated, lobulated T2-hyperintense soft-tissue mass in the anterior thigh musculature, lateral to the femoral cortex. It spans axial slices 159–275 (~11.6 cm craniocaudal), with a maximum cross-section of roughly 2 × 2.5 cm, tapering to small bright dots at both poles — the appearance of a myxoid tumor (bright, multilobulated, intramuscular).

**How it was built:**
- Overview plus axial/coronal/sagittal contact sheets to survey the whole volume and distinguish the mass from the bright femoral vessels (which are tubular/ring-like, adjacent to the bone) and from subcutaneous/joint fluid.
- Initial single positive point on the lesion core (v1, 10.1 mL).
- A second positive point on the superior lobule (v2, 26.7 mL), which the model extended along the full hyperintense stripe seen in sagittal and coronal views.
- Verified in all three planes: the outline follows the bright tissue in the sagittal (148) and coronal (147) zoomed views; rejected the only automatic candidate (C1, normal muscle lateral to the mask); confirmed that the small round structure just past the inferior end is a vessel-like ring, so the taper points were accepted as the lesion's true ends.

Confidence is medium: the lesion extent along the fascial/vascular plane is the main uncertainty, as the mass tapers gradually into adjacent bright vascular structures at both poles.
